business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-End Loose-Leaf Tea Service and Cultural Ceramic Salons

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (national-level commercial registry administered by GAFI; no sub-state or free-zone incorporation is selected for this LLC)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Mixed Civil Law (French/Napoleonic-inspired codified system, with Sharia as a principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Constitution)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 22 of 2016; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 953 of 2003, as amended; EMLCU Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Ownership Rules; Unified Companies Law No. 64 of 2022 and its Executive Regulations (including beneficial owner identification obligations in the incorporation file); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI registration procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Registry Extract of each foreign corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry in the founder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Egypt acceded to the 1961 Apostille Convention on 14 March 2022); consular legalization where the origin state is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of each corporate founder showing ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating commercial registry or notarial authority in the founder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn Arabic translation prepared by a licensed Egyptian translator and notarized before the Egyptian Notary Public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national ID of each natural person UBO (25% or greater ownership or control)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authority of the UBO's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of copies plus sworn Arabic translation; apostille/consular legalization of the notarial certificate only where GAFI or the bank requires it

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank capital deposit certificate or source-of-funds bank statement covering the LLC's paid-in capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Egyptian bank or the founder's licensed foreign bank (correspondent) used for the capital remittance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-certified statement with apostille/consular legalization where required by GAFI; otherwise bank letterhead certification with sworn Arabic translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporation representative and first manager of the LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Notary Public if signed in Egypt, or a competent foreign notary with apostille
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign-signed POA plus sworn Arabic translation; countersignature by an Egyptian legal draftsman

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, managers, authorized signatories and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated List, Egypt's domestic terrorism designations under Law No. 8 of 2015, and the EMLCU sanctions registry; enhanced due diligence is required for any Politically Exposed Person (foreign, domestic or international-organization PEP, and family members or close associates), including documented source of wealth and source of funds; adverse media and negative news screening is executed at onboarding and re-run at each material ownership change; the LLC must appoint an AML compliance officer once operations commence and retain all CDD records for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_threshold_note: UBO means any natural person ultimately owning or controlling 25% or more of the LLC through direct or indirect shareholding, voting rights, or other control mechanisms; beneficial ownership details are filed with GAFI and the company file, accessible to the EMLCU, tax authorities, and licensed banks on a confidential basis, never published in the public commercial register extract.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_procedure: Where legal entities appear in the ownership chain, GAFI and the onboarding Egyptian bank require the chain to be elevated until a natural person is identified; a declaration of beneficial ownership signed by the founders must accompany the incorporation file, and nominee or bearer-share structures are prohibited for the LLC.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_record_keeping: The LLC must maintain a current register of beneficial owners at its registered office, updated within 15 days of any change, and produce it to competent authorities immediately upon written request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI electronic name reservation service operated through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones One-Stop-Shop (www.gafi.gov.eg) and the Commercial Registry under the Egyptian Ministry of Justice; the name clearance is obtained before filing of the incorporation application.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The LLC name must be written in Arabic letters and may include, as a secondary element, a Latin transliteration; every name must end with the legal form 'شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة' or its abbreviation; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any registered trade name, trademark, or company in the Commercial Register, and must not describe a business field not included in the company's purposes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: مصر / المصري (Egypt / Egyptian) unless expressly authorized by the registration authority
أي اسم هيئة سيادية (Name of any sovereign state body)
مبيدات حشرية أو سامة (Pesticides / Toxic substance) requiring ministerial approval
أسماء جهات أجنبية (Foreign country or state names without consent)
كلمات مخلة بالنظام العام أو الآداب (Words contrary to public order or morality)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Commercial Registry refuses a proposed name, the applicant receives a written refusal with the legal ground; the applicant may file an administrative appeal in Arabic with GAFI within 15 working days of the refusal, attaching the preliminary name search report and an explanation of distinctiveness; GAFI must reconsider within 5 working days; if the administrative appeal is rejected or the authority remains silent, the applicant may file before the competent administrative court (State Council) within 60 days of the deemed rejection; a reserved name may be renewed before expiry by paying the prescribed renewal fee for an additional 60-day period, provided the incorporation file has been initiated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_search_methodology: The request covers a phonetic and exact-match search of the Arabic name, the Latin transliteration, and a divergence-similarity check against active companies, dissolved companies within the opposition window, registered trademarks, and pending name reservations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in Egypt is mandatory for the LLC; virtual offices and co-working desks are not accepted by GAFI as the statutory seat, and the tea lounge's operating license under ISIC 5630 requires a dedicated commercial premises with a notarized lease contract registered with the district municipality and stamped by the tax authority; a virtual address may only be used for auxiliary correspondence and not for the registered office or the municipality licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.substance_requirement: The LLC must maintain in Egypt its registered office, books of account, and statutory registers; for the tea salon the municipality, health authorities, and civil defense may conduct unannounced inspections before granting and during validity of the operating license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 and Law No. 94 of 2015 (Ease of Doing Business), Articles 1-32, 47-58, 88-94; Executive Regulations thereof (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2980 of 1981, as amended)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade – General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Registration Department (Commercial Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract (Aqd al-Ta’sis) and Memorandum of Association (al-Nizam al-Asasi), filed via GAFI's electronic portal and attested before the Notary Public (Shahr al-'Aqari)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for LLCs; however, a paid-up share capital of at least EGP 6,500 is recommended for bank account opening and commercial registry purposes. Share capital subscriptions must be paid into an escrow bank account opened at an Egyptian licensed bank; the bank certificate of paid capital is required prior to final GAFI approval and commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation of the Company be and is hereby ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the capital subscriptions of the initial shareholders, as set forth in the Memorandum of Association, are approved, and the paid-up capital shall be held in escrow at a licensed Egyptian bank until the Commercial Registry issues the incorporation certificate. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is established at its designated address in Cairo, Egypt, and that the Chairman or Managing Director may execute leases and utility agreements for such office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the undersigned Manager/Governing Director is appointed as the first Manager. RESOLVED FINALLY, that the Manager is authorized to complete all filings, obtain the commercial register extract, tax card, and industrial licenses, and to open corporate bank accounts with authority to sign.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Legal Entity Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) / GAFI Electronic Portal (https://www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct online name search to verify availability and confirm compliance with naming regulations (no Islamic or politically sensitive references; must include 'LLC' or 'Limited Liability Company'). Submit the proposed name(s) with the initial incorporation application. Pay the reservation fee. Upon approval, maintain the reserved name for the statutory validity period.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all founding shareholders
Power of attorney for local incorporation agent (or founding shareholder who is resident in Egypt)
Primary and secondary name reservation certificates (if issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an objection to GAFI's legal affairs department with alternative names; amend the name reservation online within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Notarize and Execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public at the Ministry of Justice / GAFI Legal Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic-language Memorandum of Association (MoA) and Articles of Association including shareholders, capital allocation, registered office address, management structure, and business object (activities covering specialty loose-leaf tea service, cultural ceramic tea salon, beverages, confectionery service, and retail sale of tea wares). Print on stamped paper, appear before the Notary Public with each shareholder or attorney-in-fact, sign all pages, and obtain notarized certified copy. The MoA must be stamped and certified to enable subsequent commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney if any shareholder signs remotely or through agent
Valid national ID or passport of every shareholder and manager
Reserved name certificate for EG__EG__EG_LLC entity
Tax identification number for any corporate shareholder (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notary queries a discrepancy, amend the MoA text and re-submit the corrected draft to the notary office for re-stamping and signature; additional notary fees may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Escrow Capital Account and Deposit Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (e.g. National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, Commercial International Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate escrow account in the entity's name at the chosen licensed bank. Deposit the agreed paid-up capital to meet the bank's minimum balance requirements. Obtain the official bank capital deposit certificate (certificate of paid-up capital) indicating the LLC name, deposits, and account number. This certificate must be presented to GAFI for issuance of the commercial registry certificate. No withdrawals from the escrow account may be completed until the Commercial Registry certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Draft or notarized Memorandum of Association
Passport/national IDs of signatories and authorized manager(s)
GAFI pre-approval or initial incorporation application number
Lease contract or proof of registered office address (preliminary/conditional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete records, provide revised KYC documentation, obtain a tax card application reference, or address the compliance officer's additional questions; also ensure the entity name matches the name reservation exactly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Application and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) / Egyptian Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full application on the GAFI OSS platform along with notarized MoA, board resolution, capital deposit certificate, registered office lease, and manager's declarations. Pay state incorporation fees and the commercial registration stamp taxes. Upon substantive review, GAFI approves the incorporation and issues the Commercial Registry Certificate (Certificate of Incorporation) incorporating the LLC, which is transmitted to the Commercial Registry office.
required_dossiers: Notarized and stamped Memorandum of Association
First Board Resolution (ratifying formation, capital subscription, office address, appointments)
Bank certificate of paid-up capital
Certified copy of the registered office lease deed or ownership certificate
Valid IDs and address proofs of shareholders and the appointed manager
Original stamp duty receipts and GAFI fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query on the business scope, file an amended MoA with a more detailed ISIC-aligned description of the specialty tea salon and cultural ceramics lounge activity. If capital documentation is incomplete, resubmit the corrected bank certificate. Full cure within 15 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Statutory Notice in the Official Journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Commercial Registry Certificate is issued, prepare a statutory summary notice of incorporation containing the LLC name, registration number, registered office, capital, and manager, and submit it to the Official Gazette for publication. This is a legal requirement to perfect formation toward third parties. Obtain the Gazette issue excerpt and keep it in the company records.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Commercial Registry Certificate
Incorporation application summary / GAFI final approval decree
Manager's valid ID and signature specimen
Receipt of gazette publication fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette office requests corrections, supply a revised notice containing the exact registration data and re-submit in the same reporting period; late publication is cured by payment of late fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Resident Taxpayer Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Commercial Registry Certificate and the notarized MoA to the ETA to obtain a corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN) and a Provisional Tax Card. Complete the tax registration form, declaring the company's activity as a specialty tea salon, beverage service establishment and related retail. To meet VAT and operating requirements, the entity also registers for Sales/Value Added Tax (VAT Law No. 67 of 2016) if taxable supplies exceed or will exceed the registration threshold.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry Certificate (original and copies)
Notarized MoA
Copy of manager's national ID
Lease deed of registered office
Bank account statement/capital deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA rejects activity code classification, file an application for re-classification under ISIC 5630 with the proper supporting operational description; this is cured by presenting the GAFI-approved business object in the MoA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After tax registration, register the entity and its manager and expected employees with the local NASSI office. Submit the social insurance forms, employment status questionnaire, and the wage schedule. Obtain the insurance registration number. This step is necessary for any LLC with local hiring and for compliance with labor law requirements before operations start.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry Certificate
Tax Card or TIN certificate
Manager's ID card and passport photo
Lease deed of registered office
Employment forms and salary declarations for the manager (and any initial staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is queried due to missing employee declarations, file an addendum with corrected payroll information and the employees' IDs; the insurance office allows correction without penalty if filed before inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Industrial Development Authority (IDA) / General Department of Commercial and Industrial Registration at the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial and Operational License for Café, Tea Salon and Beverage Service Establishment (Rukhset al-Tashghil al-Tijari wal-Sina'i)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Limited Environmental Assessment / Registration) – small-scale food and beverage service establishment requiring submission of an Environmental Impact Assessment form and compliance with waste and wastewater management guidelines; no full EIA report required for a tea lounge with kitchenette/confectionery service but will require a simplified environmental inspection checklist approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds under Law 4/1994 and its amendments (Law 9/2009 and Law 202/2020): treated wastewater discharge to municipal sewer must meet Egyptian code limits for BOD5 < 300 mg/L, TSS < 350 mg/L, oil and grease < 50 mg/L, pH 6-9; HVAC and ventilation systems must not exceed ambient nuisance standard for particulate matter; local exhaust for tea/coffee roasting (if on-site) must meet PM10 emission limit of 150 mg/m3; sound levels inside the lounge not to exceed 80 dBA; solid waste (tea residue, broken ceramics) must be segregated and transferred to municipal waste authority under approved waste handling protocols.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) confirming compliance with fire alarm and extinguisher installation, evacuation plan, and kitchen suppression system for the tearoom/preparation kitchen. Additionally, obtain a structural load inspection and workplace occupational clearance from the competent municipality (Hayy district office) verifying premises structural soundness for public assembly use, capacity limits, and compliance with sanitary and ventilation requirements. The manager must present the approved occupancy license and obtain a waiver or clearance from the labor authority for employee workplace safety and occupational health.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), established under Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 108 of 2021 as the single national tax administration under the Ministry of Finance. Primary e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing platform: https://einvoice.gov.eg; mandatory e-receipt platform: https://ereceipt.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a locally incorporated Egyptian LLC: (1) incorporate through GAFI One-Stop Shop and obtain Commercial Registry certificate; (2) within 30 days of commencing activity, apply to the competent ETA district office for the statutory Tax Card, which embeds the TIN (national tax identification number); (3) file VAT registration where annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed EGP 500,000 (compulsory) or where turnover exceeds EGP 50,000 (voluntary election); (4) onboard into the ETA e-invoicing/e-receipt environment by registering the Tax Card, obtaining ETA digital certificates, and testing the API integration. For a non-resident foreign entity with no Egyptian establishment, obtain a direct ETA TIN/VAT ID, appoint a tax representative in Egypt, and, if carrying on a trade in Egypt through a fixed place, register the branch/permanent establishment with GAFI and the ETA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Egypt does not provide U.S.-style check-the-box elections, partnership-transparency elections for LLCs, or hybrid-mismatch elections. The Egyptian LLC is mandatorily classified as a resident juridical person taxed at entity level under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and is separately assessed; group relief or consolidated taxation is unavailable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, and its Executive Regulations (Ministerial Decree No. 517 of 2016), administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration when annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000; voluntary registration available where annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 50,000; inclusion in the mandatory e-invoice/e-receipt regime is phased by turnover and applies to all VAT-registered taxpayers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing (B2B/B2G) and e-receipts (B2C) via ETA-authorised platforms: all VAT-registered taxpayers must issue invoices/receipts in ETA-defined XML/JSON schemas and transmit them near-real-time through REST APIs authenticated with ETA digital certificates; each document receives a digital stamp comprising a unique UUID, electronic signature (KID), and QR code; the ETA validates and clears documents electronically, rejects non-compliant documents, and compares declared output VAT with the buyer's input VAT ledger, with penalties for delayed, missing, or altered fiscal documents.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 10 of Law No. 67 of 2016 applies to: (a) tangible goods physically exported from Egypt, provided the goods are exported within ninety (90) days from the date of supply (or such extended period as the ETA approves) and the sale is settled in foreign currency repatriated to Egypt within one hundred and eighty (180) days; (b) services rendered for the account of a non-resident where the benefit of the service is consumed entirely outside Egypt; and (c) qualifying supplies to designated free zones. A specialty tea salon/lounge exporting packaged tea or rendering tea-ceremony services abroad must be VAT-registered, hold contemporaneous export documentation, and maintain a complete audit trail of foreign-currency receipts to sustain the 0% rate and claim input VAT refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (final certified export entry) evidencing legal exportation of the goods
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) with corresponding packing list
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency in an Egyptian bank account within 180 days
Commercial export invoice, signed sales contract or purchase order
Certificate of Origin plus any phytosanitary/food-safety export certificate required for tea and food-contact ceramic products
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA export-audit scrutiny is stringent: failure to prove physical export within 90 days, failure to repatriate proceeds within 180 days, or submission of false, backdated, or fabricated export papers causes retroactive recharacterisation of the zero-rated supply as a domestic taxable supply at 14% VAT, with assessment of the VAT plus monthly late-payment additional tax of 2% per month (statutorily capped), fines of EGP 5,000-50,000 per violation under Law 67 of 2016, clawback of any input VAT refunded or offset through the exporter ledger, fiscal-file suspension or revocation of e-invoice digital certificates, and criminal tax-evasion liability (imprisonment and/or fines) for fraudulent zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - also exercising delegated foreign exchange administration powers under Law No. 194 of 2020 and the 1982 Foreign Exchange Law, as amended by Decree No. 24 of 2021.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a heavily managed floating exchange regime. Current account transactions are largely convertible: imports, services, royalties, and profit remittances may be routed through CBE-licensed commercial banks without prior CBE approval provided documentary evidence (invoice, tax card, contract) is submitted. Capital account transactions require CBE approval: inbound foreign direct investment is facilitated via registration with CBE on the MISR (Investment) system, but outward remittances of divestment proceeds, loan repayments, and dividends are subject to source-of-funds verification and CBE registration of the original inward remittance. Profit remittance hurdles are moderate but require prompt filing of annual audited financials, tax clearance certificate, and CBE Form 12/13. In practice, hard-currency liquidity pressure in Egypt may cause administrative delays and dividend remittance prioritization by the CBE; as of 2025, there is no blanket ban but banks may impose de facto rationing during shortages. No forced surrender of receipts from current account services is currently applied, but all FX inflows must be repatriated and credited to a CBE-authorized account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be fully repatriated to Egypt within six (6) months from the date of shipment per CBE Circular No. 86 of November 2022 (amended by CBE Circular of April 2024). The mandatory conversion ratio is currently 0% - exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in foreign currency in their domiciled foreign currency accounts at a CBE-licensed bank, provided they provide the original customs bill of lading, the export declaration, and an attested invoice/service contract. However, the CBE may, from time to time, impose a temporary 50% surrender requirement (as was done between March and November 2023); current market conditions indicate the surrender mandate is suspended. Failure to repatriate within the 6-month timeline triggers a civil penalty of 0.2% of the unremitted amount per week and loss of export license benefits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_controls_risk_standing: Egypt is classified by the IMF as a jurisdiction with moderate capital controls. The CBE maintains a 'negative list' of prohibited capital transactions and requires that all cross-border transactions be effected through Authorized Dealers. For treasury planning, the LLC must obtain a CBE-approved 'dealing reference' and comply with monthly reporting of foreign transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.professional_recommendation: Issue all cross-border contracts with a foreign currency choice-of-law clause, price in USD or EUR, and obtain CBE prior approval for any shareholder loan above USD 1,000,000 equivalent. Engage an external FX consultant to monitor CBE circulars on a weekly basis due to the volatile regulatory environment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.further_detail_note: The CBE's 'Subsidiary and Branch Bank Account' opening requirements are documented in CBE Board of Directors Decree No. 1 of 2023, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.clearing_modernization_factor: Egypt has implemented RTGS (real-time gross settlement) via the 'RTGS' system operated by the CBE; cross-border transfers require final settlement in US Dollars through New York clearing, Euro via Target 2, and EGP via the CBE's 'MisRRT' system. This materially affects liquidity clearing rails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.deadline_compliance_flag: Board must calendar the 6-month export repatriation deadline and the monthly CBE reporting cycle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.fx_regulatory_instrument_availability: The CBE does not currently license NDF trading onshore; trade transactions may use plain cross-currency forwards only via Authorized Dealers. Prudent hedges should be contracted with a top-tier onshore bank, not an offshore entity, to avoid penalties under the 1982 Law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.relevant_eg_tax_bracket_insight: The corporate income tax rate is 22.5%, and dividend remittances to foreign shareholders are subject to a 10% withholding tax (if not reduced by treaty). For Egypt, the US-Egypt tax treaty is in force, but a US treaty claim is not required for trade remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.composite_rating: Moderate regulatory risk: legal capital and dividend repatriation is permitted but administrative delays occur; strategic approach is to maintain dual liquidity buffers (onshore and offshore) using intercompany loan structures approved by the CBE.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EGP + USD) for daily trade settlements and capacity for domestic retail card acquiring
Operational Account (EGP + EUR/GBP, useful for tea import sourcing from UK/China)
Operational Account + Foreign Currency Savings Account; CIB is the strongest for cross-border SWIFT liquidity and export documentary collection

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: QNB Al Ahly (Qatar National Bank SAE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Non-Resident subsidiary of QNB; may be used for dual-currency account if the shareholders are GCC nationals
Cross-border Cash Management Account (MT940/942) and trade finance LC capability
Capital Escrow Account used for inward remittance registration with CBE, especially for foreign direct investment certificate issuance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low. Egyptian law (Law No. 194 of 2020, as amended) reserves deposit-taking and payment facilitation from Egyptian residents to banks and licensed payment service providers (PSPs) authorized by CBE. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, Currencycloud) have no passporting right into Egypt; they can only be used on a complementary basis outside Egypt for receiving non-resident settlement accounts, but they cannot be the primary operating account for the LLC in Egypt. In practice, CBE wire transfers require a Correspondent Bank relationship which outlaw EMIs. Acceptable only if the entity simultaneously holds a full-service Egyptian bank account and uses the EMI as an ancillary FX conversion tool. Recommendation: avoid structuring bank account hierarchy with an EMI as 'lead'. If used, ensure the EMI is candorally disclosed to CBE and the substance requirements of the Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Financing of Terrorism Law No. 80 of 2002 (amended) are met.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: All legal representatives (Chairman, Managing Director) and actual beneficial owners (UBOs) exercising control over the LLC must appear physically before the bank's compliance department for an in-person interview in Egypt. Remote video KYC is not accepted by any tier-1 Egyptian bank; bankers require a physical presence for signature and biometric capture (fingerprint) due to CBE's Know Your Customer Addendum No. 1/2021. Additionally, the original constitutional documents must be presented in apostilled/court-notarized form. No fully digital remote onboarding is available for a foreign-owned Egyptian LLC. A proxy with a special power of attorney (an anchor attorney in Egypt) may attend the interview if all UBOs cannot travel, but each UBO must still complete a certified notice of no-objection and appear via video link with bank's interviewed branch in real time. Often the bank asks for two visits: one to deposit minimum capital and one for final account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-Risk Jurisdiction IP considerations - the specialty tea salon imports high-value loose-leaf tea from China, Sri Lanka, and Kenya, countries that may be flagged on internal bank watchlists for trade finance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade route documentation: full bill of lading (three original copies), CFDA import permit and customs clearance certificate, the issuing chamber of commerce origin certificate, and authenticated vendor Due Diligence report (background passed). Provide also: Factory inspection report in the exporting country, quality certificates (ISO 7116 for frucele tea? Actually ISO 3720 for black tea) and proof of indirect shipping via a neutral transshipment hub (e.g., Jebel Ali or Port Said) to avoid direct high-risk country routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth for settlor/beneficiary: The LLC is capitalized via shareholder remittance from a foreign entity with unclear ultimate parent chain (conditions on non-resident ownership of 100% allowed).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate formation certificate (Capital Declaration), certificate of incumbency, UBO registry extraction, board resolution authorizing the transfer, cancellation proof of the source bank account, and a personal wealth declaration letter signed by each shareholder with bank references. Obtain a tax residence certificate (Egyptian Ministry of Finance) if those shareholders are themselves Egyptian residents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent business activity vs Aligned commercial model: Use of cash-heavy retail POS collection for specialty tea lounge that later receives intercompany management fees from a foreign parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Financial projections and pricing model: retail POS sales slips aggregation, Egyptian sales tax receipt system (E-ticket) registration, monthly management-fee invoices, and executed intercompany service agreement with same grain (transfer pricing) documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected counterparty - foreign shareholder uses a shell company registered in a tax haven (e.g., British Virgin Islands) as funding vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The bank may reject shell entities entirely if no physical substance. Defense: Provide bank letters from regional local advisors, economic substance evidence (local employment in BVI if required), or restructure funding from the direct beneficial owner's operating company entity located in a middle-east hub like UAE. If feasible, alter the shareholder base to have at least one natural person as a signatory to reduce trigger severity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.onboarding_documentation_matrix: Complete list - (1) Certificate of Incorporation (MoI) and Commercial Registry Extract; (2) Tax card and Tax clearance certificate (NIF); (3) Investment authority license; (4) Lease agreement of the salon premises; (5) Board resolution authorizing bank account opening and designated signatories; (6) Passport copies of each authorized signatory and UBO; (7) Reference letter from existing bank (if historical); (8) Proof of registered office address (utility bill).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a foreign-owned Egyptian LLC, inbound equity capital must be routed via a CBE-licensed Authorized Dealer bank in Egypt using SWIFT MT103 wire transfer. The sender must clearly quote the CBE investment code 'Capital Import for Direct Investment - Employment Service' (purpose code 401) plus the independent inbound reference number assigned by the CBE's 'Capital Registration' system. The Egyptian bank will generate a 'Inward Remittance Confirmation Letter' (Form 39) within 5 business days and register the capital on the CBE's Foreign Investment database, crucial for future profit/dividend repatriation. For loans: another purpose code '901' (Foreign Loan) must be filed, and the lender must submit a CBE loan declaration, after which the loan can be imported through the same channel. All wires must be in USD, EUR, or GBP; no EGP is permitted for foreign capital injection. Verification: the bank will ask for signed audited financial statements, the LLC's articles of association, and proof of the underlying tea-salon business activity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for importing tea leaf, manufacturing raw ceramics, and lounge operational supplies should be cleared using the following rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct-supplier wires under USD 500,000; (b) Sight Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) for larger purchase orders - available at CIB, Banque Misr, NBE - confirmed irrevocable L/C issued by the Egyptian importer's bank, with payment term up to 120 days; (c) Documentary Collection (D/P or D/A) with Bill of Lading; and (d) for recurring domestic supplier payments, use the Egyptian National Payment System (NPBS) via local Chequand e-clearing. In all cases, the Egyptian customs invoice (Export Invoice) must be dated and stamped by the bank. To avoid penalties, use the correct CBE 'Trade Goods' purpose code (e.g., 0001/200) and attach the commercial contract, commercial invoice, bill of lading, and Egypt Customs import declaration (AZID). Petty outbound operational expense (e.g., server fees) can be settled using MT103 with purpose code '0030' (services), but require the supplying company to provide a Tax Registration Certificate issued in their country.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (plain-vanilla, onshore with CBE Authorized Dealer, tenor up to 12 months, underlying cross-border trade documentation required; not allowed for speculative positions)
Cross-Currency Swaps for matching states (limited & only available through investment-grade counterparties; bank may require CBE derogation)

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - legally not permissible for Egyptian resident entities to directly originate; however, Shell-Branch or offshore sister company may hedge on behalf of the Egyptian sub solely for internal netting, transacted outside Egypt.
Currency Options (calls/puts) are permissible only by special approval from CBE's Market Operations Department; typical thesps of tea salons cannot secure them due to low liquidity classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.clearing_rail_technology_note: For same-day USD settlement with Egyptian banks, route via New York Clearing House Interbank Payments System (CHIPS) or Fedwire; use the instruction 'RULE/DOC. AGAINST PAYMENT' on the MT103. For EUR, use Target2. For EGP cross-border? not applicable - EGP is not fully convertible offshore. The LLC should open a sub-account for e-commerce with the licenced PSP Baer - if required by the lounge.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_optimization_strategy: Maintain a dual-currency bank structure: an EGP operating account for payroll and local excise, and a USD account for import transactions. Do not route EGP through an offshore clearing provider. Negotiate a 'Sweep and Lynx' arrangement with CIB that converts excess EGP cash into USD-controlled daily block for trade settlements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.treasury_governance_recommendation: Appoint an internal treasury officer (personal finance endorsement) responsible for ESR(FX) reporting to the CBE within 10 working days after each month-end, track notional FX exposure, and set a corporate policy not to hold more than $100,000 unhedged at any given time for a turnover under $1 million.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.contingency_rails_documentation: If SWIFT channel is interrupted (e.g., US-sanctioned Corridor), use a special Correspondent bank via Emirati Bank (e.g., First Abu Dhabi Bank) as an intermediary to transfer USD to the local Egyptian bank. This is permissible only if the transaction is not on the CBE outward remittance restriction list and the ultimate beneficial owner information is fully shared with both banks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 41) and annual reconciliation of withheld salaries tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end; April 30 of the following year for the standard December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delay penalty of 2% of the unpaid tax for the first six months and 2.5% per month thereafter; late-filing fines of EGP 5,000-50,000 under Tax Procedures Law No. 206/2020; persistent default triggers coercive collection, tax-card suspension, and contributes to GAFI administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements, manager's report, and minutes of the partners' annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end (June 30 for December 31 year-end); annual general meeting of partners must be convened in the same window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managerial fines of up to EGP 50,000 (approx. USD 1,000) under Companies Law No. 159/1981; failure to file annual accounts for two consecutive years supports GAFI administrative de-registration and strike-off after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry (GAFI One-Stop Shop counter)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the original commercial registration; renewal payment and declaration filed within the 30 days preceding the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating overdue fees of EGP 100-1,000 and a 'dormant' registry flag after one year of non-renewal; continued non-renewal is statutory grounds for mandatory administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI / Commercial Registry (AML oversight by the Financial Regulatory Authority and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit - EMLCU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually together with the audited financial statements (within six months of fiscal year-end); interim UBO updates required within 30 days of any registered share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EGP 100,000 (approx. USD 2,000) for false or untimely UBO disclosures; unupdated registers invalidate share-transfer entries and can freeze dividend distribution and GAFI good-standing certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly Value-Added Tax declaration and settlement (12 filings per calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 30th day of the month following each monthly tax period; every calendar month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory delay charge on unpaid VAT plus fixed late-filing penalties under Law No. 206/2020; recurring delinquency triggers tax-card suspension, asset attachment, and input-VAT credit disallowance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly payroll (salaries tax) withholding return and social insurance contribution statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (salaries tax) and Social Insurance Authority (SIA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly; salaries-tax remittance due by the 15th day of the month following the payroll month; social insurance contributions due by the last day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Salaries-tax delay penalty of 2% monthly for the first six months and 2.5% monthly thereafter; social insurance late-payment interest, execution measures, and travel restrictions against managers for sustained non-payment; unreported wages disallowed as tax deductions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory annual audit by an Egyptian certified public accountant registered with the Accountants Syndicate applies when paid-in capital equals or exceeds EGP 100,000, annual turnover equals or exceeds EGP 1,000,000, or a GAFI investment license is held; in practice, any VAT-registered LLC with annual supplies exceeding the EGP 500,000 compulsory VAT registration threshold must file audited statements with ETA and GAFI. A specialty tea-salon lounge accepting POS and credit-card payments normally exceeds this revenue threshold, making the independent annual audit mandatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by the Minister of Investment and substantially aligned with IFRS; consolidated group accounts must comply with EAS; foreign-parent groups may present supplementary IFRS packagings while statutory books remain in EAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a Register of Beneficial Owners showing every natural person holding more than 25% of equity, voting control, or senior-manager control. Share transfers must be reflected in the register and in the GAFI commercial file within 30 days; the manager submits an annual confirmation declaration with the audited financial statements, affirming the UBO schedule to be current, complete, and consistent with AML customer-due-diligence records held by the entity.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per year for a Cairo/Giza registered office and licensed corporate agent, including GAFI data-update handling and registered-office address services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for an Egyptian CPA independent audit of a small to mid-size food-and-beverage LLC with ETA and GAFI reporting requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying micro/small enterprises may elect the Law 152/2020 simplified turnover tax regime at 0.5% to 1.5% of gross revenue, provided annual turnover does not exceed EGP 10 million. No statutory tax holiday applies to a standard inland specialty tea salon; limited credits may become available for employment of disabled workers and certain training expenditures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via the Egyptian Tax Authority e-Tax portal (www.incometax.gov.eg)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional prepayment returns may be due for taxpayers subject to self-assessment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end (Article 69, Law 91 of 2005)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: company name, tax card number, commercial registration, headquarters address and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian permanent-establishment address as per registration and identify the foreign parent entity in the supplementary ownership schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period: start and end dates covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the PE business accounting period as approved; if the tax year differs from the foreign head office year, file within the Egyptian PE reporting cycle unless a waiver is obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all sources, including tea sales, salon service receipts, cultural-event fees, and retail merchandise.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare Egypt-sourced gross revenue as well as any foreign-source profit attributable to the Egyptian PE. All revenue from the tea-salon operation is subject to Egyptian tax irrespective of the foreign owner's residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: cost of tea inventory, employee payroll, rent, utilities, depreciation on POS/kitchen equipment, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only direct and clearly supported Egyptian PE expenses; cross-charged group costs must be documented with invoices, contracts, and arm's-length justification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable business income: accounting net result adjusted for non-deductible reserves, entertainment expenses, and tax disallowances under Law 91 of 2005.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the Egyptian statutory profit with foreign GAAP/IFRS, and add back non-deductible expenses such as unsubstantiated management fees or head-office allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax liability settlement: application of the 22.5% headline rate, available prepayment credit, and final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only treaty or domestic reductions against Egyptian-sourced income; the final liability must be settled in EGP into the Egyptian Tax Authority account before the deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers a monthly delay surcharge of 2% of the unpaid tax (with a cumulative ceiling generally applied), plus an administrative fine ranging from EGP 500 to EGP 5,000; further non-compliance may extend to a criminal fine up to EGP 20,000 and asset seizures for confirmed evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% of the gross cash dividend paid to residents and non-residents (Article 56, Law 91 of 2005); a 10% domestic final withholding applies on profit distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholders must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by their country of residence (generally not older than six months) together with an Egyptian Treaty Relief Application, an annual dividend certificate, and supporting evidence of beneficial ownership. The Egyptian Tax Authority reviews the application and issues a clearance/endorsement; if relief is not pre-approved, the payer must withhold at the domestic 10% rate and the non-resident may claim a refund through a revised return or mutual agreement procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding tax for royalties and periodic interest paid to non-residents is 20% (Article 58, Law 91 of 2005); under Egypt's double-tax treaties the rates can be reduced to 10–15% for royalties, and 10–15% for interest, subject to LOB/principal-purpose tests and the TRC protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is mandatory when aggregate related-party controlled transactions exceed EGP 5,000,000 during the tax year; Master File obligations arise when the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds EGP 45,000,000. The Egyptian Tax Authority may nevertheless request TP documentation case-by-case regardless of these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egyptian tax law embeds a substance-over-form GAAR (Article 9, Law 91 of 2005) and a broad permanent-establishment definition. There is no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE, but the tea salon must evidence physical premises, engaged employees, actual management decisions, and genuine operational activity in Egypt to uphold treaty residency claims and avoid re-characterisation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating tea-salon cash receipts, recording nominee sales volumes, fabricating supplier invoices for tea leaves, or inflating depreciation and payroll to erase taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to two to five times the evaded tax, imprisonment for up to five years, judicial re-assessment, interest on unpaid tax, and forced attachment of company assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax; a conviction triggers travel bans, property seizure, and imprisonment for the signatory officer; the corporate veil is pierced where bad faith is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the LLC nominally as a tea lounge to divert invoiced income to a foreign treasury entity, to obtain treaty benefits, or to disguise capital flight under a forged service contract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR re-characterisation of the transaction, disallowance of expenses, additional WHT at 20% on deemed royalties/interest, an anti-avoidance penalty of up to 100% of the tax avoided, and possible suspension or revocation of the company's commercial registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will disregard the LLC's separate personality; directors and shareholders may be held personally liable for the entire tax debt, ordered to compensate creditors, and barred from leaving Egypt pending settlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting substantial cash deliveries without generating POS records, structuring cash holdings in small accounts to avoid the reporting threshold, or using the tea-salon cash flow to fund an unlicensed foreign venture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 80 of 2002 as amended, penalties include imprisonment from five to fifteen years, fines up to EGP 2,000,000, confiscation of proceeds, freezing of bank accounts, and possible closure of the establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers, directors, and the AML compliance officer are criminally liable absent proof of due diligence; the corporate veil is pierced for knowing participation, leading to travel bans, extradition, and personal asset forfeiture.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing related-party marketing, trademark licensing, or tea-blend research services at prices materially different from open-market benchmarks, or failing to maintain contemporaneous country-by-country and master-file records as required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A primary TP adjustment increasing taxable income, a 40% penalty levied on the adjustment amount, additional withholding tax on the reclassified distributions, and a fine for incomplete documentation under Decree 181 of 2019.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incomplete tax returns or knowingly approve non-arm's-length intercompany contracts face joint liability for the additional tax and penalties; in aggravated cases of false documentation, directors may be prosecuted for tax evasion and subjected to travel restrictions.
